rawFindings.title: lean find() no longer makes populated documents lean
rawFindings.explanation: For populated find queries this now passes the raw populate options through unchanged. When the parent query has `lean` enabled, the removed helper used to set each populate path's `options.lean = true`; without that, `Model.populate()` hydrates populated paths even though the top-level result is returned as lean.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the lean propagation here, e.g. call a helper that copies `self.options.populate` and sets `option.options.lean = true` when `options.lean` is true before calling `model.populate()`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given `Post.find().lean().populate('author').exec(cb)`, `posts[0]` is a plain object but `posts[0].author` is a Mongoose document with methods like `save`/`update`, instead of a plain object as lean population previously returned.

rawFindings.title: lean findOne() no longer makes populated documents lean
rawFindings.explanation: For populated findOne queries this now passes raw populate options to `Model.populate()` and skips the removed logic that propagated the parent query's `lean` option to populated paths. As a result, populated subdocuments are hydrated even though the findOne result itself is lean.
rawFindings.suggestion: Before calling `model.populate()`, set each populate option's `options.lean = true` when `options.lean` is true, or restore the previous `preparePopulationOptions(self, options)` helper.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given `Post.findOne().lean().populate('author').exec(cb)`, `post` is a plain object but `post.author` is a Mongoose document with methods like `save`/`update`, instead of a plain object.
